Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
hey, can you help me put together a family dinner calendar for october? i need a prompt that asks for the calendar, not a finished list of dinners right now. it is for the carter household: mara and luis, their kids nora and eli, and mara's mother june, who eats with us fairly often. we have four people at dinner most nights, sometimes five when june comes over, so please make the plan workable for that range without treating her visits as fixed. we do not know which october year this is for yet, so use the date numbers in the month but don't attach weekdays to them. i want something we can look over together and adjust, not a formal nutrition plan or a complicated cooking project.

we are mainly trying to settle dinner ahead of time, because the late afternoon conversation about what to cook keeps taking too long. make one entry for each date from 1 through 31, with the meal name and a short note if a useful detail needs explaining. a table would be easy to read on the kitchen tablet, though if a simple numbered layout is clearer that is okay too. this is a dinner calendar, not breakfast planning. a few dinners can deliberately be leftovers or a flexible night, but don't fill the month with vague entries like “something easy.” if an evening is left open for leftovers, say that plainly. the finished calendar should be usable without us having to guess what each entry means, but there is no need for full recipes.

for cooking, mara is usually home first and can start dinner, while luis gets back later and can finish something that is already underway. nora can help with chopping when asked, and eli is eight, so don't assume he can handle stove jobs. we have one oven, a standard stovetop, a rice cooker, and a slow cooker. the slow cooker is useful on days when mara has an appointment after work, but the appointments are not on a regular schedule, so don't assign that to a particular date. on ordinary work nights we want most of the active cooking to stay around thirty minutes; a longer oven time is okay if it doesn't mean someone has to stand there the whole time. sunday can be a little more relaxed, although it shouldn't turn into an elaborate special occasion meal every week.

food-wise, nora dislikes mushrooms and eli is not keen on very spicy food. please leave mushrooms out, and keep heat mild, with chili sauce or another spicy add-on kept separate if a dish can use one. nobody has a stated allergy, and june eats the same general meals as the rest of us. mara likes vegetables worked into the meal, luis would rather have a filling main dish, and the kids are more willing to try things when there is a familiar side such as rice, bread, or potatoes. we don't need every dinner to satisfy each preference equally, but keep the whole month balanced in that ordinary sense. there are no special dietary rules to build around.

we normally shop once a week, usually saturday, but there isn't a confirmed shopping day for every week in october. don't make the plan depend on exact delivery dates or ingredients that are only available on one particular day. pantry basics we usually have are rice, pasta, canned tomatoes, beans, broth, flour, and a few common dried herbs. the freezer often has chicken thighs and peas, but quantities change, so don't make those the only possible choices for several dates in a row. fresh vegetables can vary. it would help if ingredients such as herbs, greens, or a bag of potatoes appeared in more than one nearby dinner where that makes sense, so we can use them up, but no need to calculate a shopping list or claim we already have anything beyond those usual staples.

we have a loose spending target of about 150 dollars for dinners across the month, not counting pantry items already on hand. it is only a guide, not a demand for exact prices, and we understand the total can vary by store. favor ordinary affordable ingredients and don't make every meal depend on meat. a couple of vegetarian dinners are welcome, and beans are fine, but please don't turn the entire plan into a vegetarian menu. some chicken is okay too. leave enough variety that the dates don't read like the same dish renamed; repeating a familiar dinner once is fine if it helps with leftovers or a busy evening.

leftovers are useful for lunches, especially when there is enough for more than one lunch, but dinner portions should still cover four and occasionally five people. we have containers and a microwave. if a meal naturally makes extra, a brief note can say to save the extra for lunch; don't assume every recipe makes a particular number of servings or provide invented nutrition numbers. friday is often the night when the kids ask for something familiar, and a homemade pizza, pasta, or tacos would be welcome sometimes, not necessarily every friday. june likes soup, and it would be nice to have one or two soup dinners during the month if they fit, but don't make a specific visit or event out of that preference.

please keep the calendar practical and warm rather than sounding like a diet sheet. use familiar meal names and short notes; we can look up a recipe later. don't include breakfast, lunch menus, a shopping list, or full instructions for cooking. don't infer holidays, birthdays, school events, or anyone's work appointments from the month. we sometimes pass the calendar around in the family chat, and it is fine to share the text-only calendar there. do not publish photos of the family or the meals on public social media or websites. that restriction is about photos in public places; it isn't a request to hide the dinner names from our relatives. one comment from luis was, “if it can be warmed up without drying out, save me a portion for tomorrow.” finish the prompt by asking for the date-by-date october dinner calendar and keep that quote as a preference about leftovers, not as a rule that every dish must meet.", "output": "Create a practical, warm-toned family dinner calendar for October for the Carter household. Provide one entry for each date from 1 through 31, using the date numbers without weekday labels because the year is not known. Include the dinner name and a brief note where useful. The text-only calendar may be shared in the family chat. Do not publish photos of the family or the meals on public social media or websites.
